passage:
Tuesday. The bus stop was twenty minutes from Bhaskar's home, and he left at 7:40 for the 8:00 bus. Outside the temple, his classmate Mahima called him over to see a beetle. When he looked up, it was 7:52. He ran, and the doors were already closing. The conductor waved him in, and Bhaskar sat down, out of breath.

Wednesday. At breakfast his mother Kavitha noticed him staring at the wall clock. "I'll leave at half past seven," he said. "Ten extra minutes. If Mahima calls me again I can say hello and still walk."

Friday. Bhaskar left at 7:30, stopped by the temple to look at a new beetle for a few minutes, and reached the bus stop at 7:55 with time to spare.

qa.q: What did Mahima call Bhaskar over to see?
qa.a: Mahima called Bhaskar over to see a beetle.

qa.q: How was Bhaskar feeling as he ran for the bus?
qa.a: Bhaskar was worried and out of breath, afraid the bus would leave without him.

qa.q: What else could Bhaskar do if a friend calls him over again?
qa.a: Bhaskar could say he will look another time, or look quickly and check the clock first.

qa.q: How might Kavitha feel watching Bhaskar plan this himself?
qa.a: Kavitha may feel proud and relieved that Bhaskar worked out the fix without being told.

grounding: Shows a boy leaving ten minutes earlier after a friend's chat nearly made him miss the bus.

passage:
Rehana, you're always rushing for the school bus. Let your Rafiq Nana tell you what happened when I was about nine.
Our house to the bus stop was twenty minutes' walk, so I left exactly twenty minutes before the bus.
One morning my friend Iqbal stopped me outside the bakery to show me his new marbles. Only a few minutes, but when I reached the stop, the bus was pulling away. I ran behind it, waving. The conductor saw me and it stopped. I got on, red in the face, with the whole bus laughing.
That evening I decided: thirty minutes, not twenty. If nothing happens, I wait at the stop. If something happens, I still make it.
I never missed a bus after that, beti.

qa.q: How long was the walk from Rafiq's house to the bus stop?
How did Rafiq feel when he got on the bus with everyone laughing?
qa.a: He felt embarrassed, red in the face after running behind the bus.

qa.q: After nearly missing the bus, what choice did Rafiq make, and why was it wise?
qa.a: He decided to leave ten minutes earlier, so a small delay like stopping to talk would no longer make him miss the bus.

qa.q: How might Iqbal have felt if Rafiq had missed the bus?
qa.a: Iqbal might have felt guilty, since he only wanted to show his marbles and did not mean to make his friend late.

grounding: It shows a boy who takes twenty minutes to reach the bus stop choosing to leave thirty minutes early after a friend's chat nearly made him miss the bus.

subtype: Approach: leaves extra time before something starts [Action]
passage:
The school bus stop in Kalyan was a twenty-minute walk, and the monsoon had come. Last Monday, Yusuf left exactly twenty minutes before the bus. His friend Tarun stopped him at the gate to talk about cricket. Yusuf reached the stop just as the doors were closing and had to bang on them.
On Tuesday night he said to his mother, "I'm leaving at thirty minutes before."
"Why ten extra?"
"In case someone stops me. Or the road is flooded. Or I forget something."
On Wednesday, it poured, and the usual lane was knee-deep. He took the long way round. Tarun waved from a shop; Yusuf only waved back.
He reached the stop with four minutes to spare, wet but on time. The bus came. He climbed in, grinning.

qa.q: How many minutes to spare did Yusuf have on Wednesday?
qa.a: He reached the stop with four minutes to spare.

qa.q: How did Yusuf feel when he climbed onto the bus?
qa.a: He felt pleased and relieved, grinning because the extra ten minutes worked even in the rain.

qa.q: What else could Yusuf do on very rainy days, and why?
qa.a: He could leave a few minutes earlier still, since flooded lanes can use up most of the extra time.

qa.q: How might Tarun feel when Yusuf only waves back?
qa.a: Tarun may feel a little left out, but likely understands Yusuf is trying not to miss the bus.

grounding: It shows a boy who takes twenty minutes to reach the bus stop starting to leave thirty minutes before after nearly missing the bus when a friend stopped him.
